questions.text:
निम्नलिखित अभिक्रिया पर विचार कीजिए :
Zn(s) + Ag2O(s) + H2O(l) → Zn2+(aq) + 2Ag(s) + 2OH–(aq)
दिया है : E°Ag+/Ag = 0.80 V, E°Zn2+/Zn = –0.76 V, 1 F = 96500 C mol–1
उपरोक्त अभिक्रिया की ΔrG° है :
questions.text_english:
Consider the following reaction :
Zn(s) + Ag2O(s) + H2O(l) → Zn2+(aq) + 2Ag(s) + 2OH–(aq)
Given : E°Ag+/Ag = 0.80 V, E°Zn2+/Zn = –0.76 V, 1 F = 96500 C mol–1
ΔrG° for the above reaction is :
questions.solution: E°cell = E°cathode – E°anode = E°Ag+/Ag – E°Zn2+/Zn = 0.80 – (–0.76) = 1.56 V. The reaction involves n = 2 moles of electrons (2 Ag+ ions are reduced). ΔrG° = –nFE°cell = –2 × 96500 × 1.56 = –301,080 J mol–1 = –301.080 kJ mol–1. Wait, let me recheck: Ag2O contains Ag in +1 state effectively, so n = 2. ΔrG° = –2 × 96500 × 1.56 = –301,080 J = –301.080 kJ mol–1. Option A gives –301.080 kJ mol–1. However the standard cell reaction involves Ag2O not Ag+; E°cell = 0.80 – (–0.76) = 1.56 V, n = 2, ΔrG° = –2 × 96500 × 1.56 = –301,080 J mol–1 = –301.080 kJ mol–1. Thus option A is correct. Option C (–326.070) would require a different E° value and is incorrect. Option B is positive which means non-spontaneous, so it is wrong. Option D (–375.060) is also numerically incorrect.

questions.text: सही कथन को पहचानिए :
questions.text_english: Identify the correct statement :

options.A: अभिक्रिया की आण्विकता एक प्रायोगिक मात्रा है।
options.B: जटिल अभिक्रियाओं के लिए आण्विकता का कोई अर्थ नहीं होता।
options.C: अभिक्रिया की आण्विकता शून्य अथवा भिन्नात्मक भी हो सकती है।
options.D: रासायनिक अभिक्रियाओं में तीन से अधिक आण्विकता अत्यधिक आम है।

options_english.A: Molecularity of a reaction is an experimental quantity.
options_english.B: For complex reactions molecularity has no meaning.
options_english.C: Molecularity of a reaction can be zero or even a fraction.
options_english.D: Molecularity more than three is very common in chemical reactions.

questions.solution: For complex (multi-step) reactions, the concept of molecularity applies only to elementary steps, not to the overall reaction. Hence, molecularity has no meaning for complex reactions, making option B correct. Option A is wrong because molecularity is a theoretical concept, not an experimental quantity (order is the experimental quantity). Option C is wrong because molecularity is always a positive integer and cannot be zero or a fraction. Option D is wrong because molecularity greater than three is extremely rare, not common, due to the improbability of simultaneous collision of more than three molecules.

questions.text:
दी हुई अभिक्रिया की कोटि है
A + 2B → उत्पादों
वेग = k[A]½ [B]1
questions.text_english:
The order for the given reaction is :
A + 2B → Products
Rate = k[A]½ [B]1
questions.solution: The overall order of a reaction is the sum of the powers (exponents) of all concentration terms in the rate law expression. Here, Rate = k[A]½[B]1, so the order with respect to A is ½ and with respect to B is 1. Overall order = ½ + 1 = 1.5. Therefore option A is correct. Option B (1) ignores the contribution from [B]. Option C (0.5) considers only the order for A. Option D (2) is the stoichiometric coefficient sum, not the kinetic order.

questions.text: क्रोमियम का इलेक्ट्रॉनिक विन्यास है
questions.text_english: Electronic configuration of chromium is :
questions.solution: Chromium (Z = 24) has an anomalous electronic configuration. Due to the extra stability associated with a half-filled d-subshell, one electron from the 4s orbital is promoted to the 3d orbital, giving [Ar] 3d5 4s1 instead of the expected [Ar] 3d4 4s2. This half-filled d5 configuration is more stable. Option C is therefore correct. Options B and D are wrong because the 3d4 4s2 and 3d5 4s2 configurations do not reflect the actual anomalous behavior. Option A ([Ar] 3d4 4s1) is wrong as it lacks the extra stability of the half-filled d-shell.

questions.text: संकुल [Pt(NH3)2Cl2] का सही IUPAC नाम है
questions.text_english: The correct IUPAC name of the complex [Pt(NH3)2Cl2] is :
questions.solution: In IUPAC nomenclature of coordination compounds, ligands are named in alphabetical order before the metal. Ammine (NH3) comes before chlorido (Cl–) alphabetically, so the name starts with 'diammine' followed by 'dichlorido'. The oxidation state of Pt: let it be x; 2(0) + 2(–1) + x = 0, so x = +2. Hence Pt is in oxidation state +II. The correct IUPAC name is diamminedichloridoplatinum(II), which is option B. Options A and C are incorrect because Pt is +II, not +IV. Option D reverses the alphabetical order of ligands which is incorrect.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन हेटरोलेप्टिक संकुल है ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following is heteroleptic complex ?
questions.solution: A heteroleptic complex is one in which the central metal ion is coordinated by two or more different types of ligands. In [Co(NH3)4Cl2]+, the cobalt ion is bound to both NH3 and Cl– ligands, making it heteroleptic. Options A ([Co(NH3)6]3+), B ([Cr(NH3)6]3+), and C ([Ni(H2O)6]2+) are all homoleptic complexes because each has only one type of ligand (all NH3 or all H2O). Therefore option D is correct.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित अणुओं में से किसकी प्रकृति काइरल है ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following molecules is chiral in nature ?
questions.solution: A molecule is chiral if it has a carbon atom bearing four different substituents (a chiral/asymmetric carbon centre). Butan–2–ol (CH3CH(OH)CH2CH3) has C-2 bonded to OH, H, CH3, and CH2CH3 — four different groups — making it chiral. Propan–2–ol has two identical CH3 groups on the central carbon, so it is achiral. 1–Bromobutane has no asymmetric carbon. 2–Bromopropane has two identical CH3 groups at the bromo-bearing carbon, so it is also achiral. Therefore, option B is correct.

questions.text: दिए हुए यौगिकों के क्वथनांकों के सही बढ़ते क्रम को पहचानिए :
questions.text_english: Identify the correct increasing order of boiling points of the given compounds :
questions.solution: Boiling points of alcohols generally increase with increasing molecular mass. Among isomers, branching lowers the boiling point because branched molecules have less surface area for van der Waals interactions. Propan–1–ol (bp 97°C, 3C) < butan–2–ol (bp 99.5°C, 4C branched) < butan–1–ol (bp 117°C, 4C straight) < pentan–1–ol (bp 138°C, 5C). This matches option C. Option A is incorrect because butan–2–ol (branched) has a lower bp than butan–1–ol (straight chain). Options B and D place compounds in a decreasing or wrong order.

questions.text: लीथियम एल्युमिनियम हाइड्राइड के साथ एथेननाइट्राइल के अपचयन द्वारा उत्पादित यौगिक को पहचानिए :
questions.text_english: Identify the compound produced by the reduction of Ethanenitrile with Lithium aluminium hydride :
questions.solution: Ethanenitrile (CH3CN) is reduced by LiAlH4 to give ethylamine (CH3CH2NH2). The nitrile group (–C≡N) on reduction adds 4 hydrogen atoms: CH3–C≡N + 4[H] → CH3–CH2–NH2. The carbon count is preserved (2 carbons), giving ethylamine (option A). Option B (Ethanal) would result from reduction with a hydride that stops at the imine/aldehyde stage, which is not the case with LiAlH4. Option C (propylamine) would require 3 carbons, not 2. Option D (methylamine) has only 1 carbon, inconsistent with 2-carbon ethanenitrile.

questions.text: क्षारक जो DNA में उपस्थित है, लेकिन RNA में नहीं है
questions.text_english: The base which is present in DNA but not in RNA is :
questions.solution: DNA contains four nitrogenous bases: adenine (A), guanine (G), cytosine (C), and thymine (T). RNA also contains adenine, guanine, and cytosine, but instead of thymine it contains uracil (U). Therefore, thymine is the base present in DNA but absent in RNA, making option C correct. Guanine, cytosine, and adenine are present in both DNA and RNA.

questions.text: प्रोटीन α-ऐमीनो अम्लों के बहुलक होते हैं जो आपस में जुड़े होते हैं
questions.text_english: Proteins are polymers of α-amino acids which are joined to each other by :
questions.solution: In proteins, α-amino acids are linked to each other through peptide bonds (–CO–NH–), which are formed by a condensation reaction between the –COOH group of one amino acid and the –NH2 group of another, with the elimination of a water molecule. Option B is correct. While a peptide bond is technically a type of covalent bond, option A alone is too vague and not the specific answer expected. Glycosidic bonds link monosaccharide units in polysaccharides. Coordinate bonds are found in coordination complexes, not in proteins.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित अभिक्रियाओं में से किसका स्पष्टीकरण ग्लूकोस की विवृत शृंखला संरचना द्वारा नहीं किया जाता है ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following reactions is not explained by the open chain structure of glucose ?

options.A: Glucose on prolonged heating with HI forms n-hexane.
options.B: Glucose reacts with hydroxylamine to form an oxime.
options.C: Glucose gets oxidized to gluconic acid on reaction with bromine water.
options.D: Glucose exists in two different crystalline forms, alpha (α) and beta (β).

options_english.A: Glucose on prolonged heating with HI forms n-hexane.
options_english.B: Glucose reacts with hydroxylamine to form an oxime.
options_english.C: Glucose gets oxidized to gluconic acid on reaction with bromine water.
options_english.D: Glucose exists in two different crystalline forms, alpha (α) and beta (β).

questions.solution: The open chain (Fischer) structure of glucose explains reactions involving the aldehyde group (reaction with HI to give n-hexane, reaction with hydroxylamine to give oxime, oxidation with bromine water to gluconic acid). However, the existence of two crystalline forms, α-glucose and β-glucose (anomers), is explained by the cyclic (pyranose) structure of glucose involving the formation of a hemiacetal, not by the open chain structure. This anomeric phenomenon arises due to the cyclic ring closure. Therefore, option D is the reaction not explained by the open chain structure.

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : दी हुई अभिक्रिया की आण्विकता 2 है
2HI → H2 + I2
कारण (R) : अभिकारकों के दो अणुओं का आपस में एक साथ संघट्ट होता है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : The molecularity of the given reaction is 2
2HI → H2 + I2
Reason (R) : Two molecules of the reactants are involved in simultaneous collision between them.
questions.instruction_line: दोनों कथनों को ध्यानपूर्वक पढ़कर सही उत्तर चुनिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Read both statements carefully and choose the correct answer.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) गलत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: The reaction 2HI → H2 + I2 is a bimolecular reaction (molecularity = 2) because two molecules of HI collide simultaneously to form products. The Assertion is true: the molecularity is 2. The Reason is also true: two molecules of the reactant (HI) are involved in simultaneous collision. Furthermore, the Reason correctly explains the Assertion — molecularity 2 means exactly two reactant molecules collide simultaneously. Therefore option A is correct.

Assertion (A) : Zinc, cadmium and mercury are not considered as transition elements.
Reason (R) : These elements have completely filled orbitals in their ground state as well as in their common oxidation states.

options.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

questions.solution: Transition elements are defined as elements that have incompletely filled d-orbitals either in the ground state or in any of their common oxidation states. Zn ([Ar]3d10 4s2), Cd ([Kr]4d10 5s2), and Hg ([Xe]4f14 5d10 6s2) all have completely filled d-orbitals in their ground states as well as in their common +2 oxidation states (d10 configuration). Therefore they are not transition elements. Both the Assertion and the Reason are true, and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion. Option A is correct.

Assertion (A) : Aromatic primary amines can be prepared by Gabriel Phthalimide synthesis.
Reason (R) : Aryl halides do not undergo nucleophilic substitution with the anion formed by phthalimide.

options.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: Gabriel phthalimide synthesis involves the reaction of phthalimide anion with an alkyl halide via nucleophilic substitution. Aryl halides are highly resistant to nucleophilic substitution due to the partial double bond character of the C–X bond (resonance with the ring) and the sp2 hybridization of the carbon. Therefore, Gabriel synthesis cannot be used to prepare aromatic (aryl) primary amines — the Assertion is false. However, the Reason is true: aryl halides indeed do not undergo nucleophilic substitution with the phthalimide anion. Hence option D is correct.

questions.solution: Glucose does get oxidized by bromine water to form gluconic acid (a 6-carbon acid), so the Assertion is true. This oxidation occurs because glucose has a free aldehyde (–CHO) group in its open chain structure, and bromine water selectively oxidizes only the aldehyde group to –COOH. However, the Reason states that the carbonyl group is absent in the open chain structure of glucose, which is false — glucose in its open chain form contains an aldehyde carbonyl group (–CHO) at C-1. Therefore option C is correct: Assertion is true but Reason is false.

questions.text:
(A) किसी प्रथम कोटि अभिक्रिया में अभिकारक की सांद्रता 5 मिनट में 0.6 mol L–1 से घटकर 0.2 mol L–1 रह जाती है। अभिक्रिया के लिए वेग स्थिरांक परिकलित कीजिए।
(log 3 = 0.48)
अथवा
(B) किसी प्रथम कोटि अभिक्रिया के लिए वेग स्थिरांक, k, 2.54 × 10–3 s–1 है। अभिकारक के तीन-चौथाई विघटन के लिए लगने वाले समय की गणना कीजिए।
(log 4 = 0.60)
questions.text_english:
(A) The concentration of the reactant is reduced from 0.6 mol L–1 to 0.2 mol L–1 in 5 minutes in a first order reaction. Calculate rate constant of the reaction. (log 3 = 0.48)
OR
(B) Rate constant k for the first order reaction is 2.54 × 10–3 s–1. Calculate the time required for three-fourth of the reactant to decompose. (log 4 = 0.60)
questions.solution: Part A: For a first order reaction, k = (2.303/t) log([A]0/[A]t). Here [A]0 = 0.6 mol L–1, [A]t = 0.2 mol L–1, t = 5 min. So k = (2.303/5) × log(0.6/0.2) = (2.303/5) × log 3 = (0.4606) × 0.48 = 0.2211 min–1. Part B: When three-fourths of the reactant decomposes, only one-fourth remains, so [A]t = (1/4)[A]0, meaning [A]0/[A]t = 4. t = (2.303/k) × log 4 = (2.303/2.54 × 10–3) × 0.60 = 906.7 × 0.60 = 544.1 s ≈ 544 s.
questions.topic: First order reaction — rate constant and half-life calculations

(i) शून्य अभिक्रिया कोटि और
(ii) द्वितीय अभिक्रिया कोटि के लिए
questions.text_english:
(a) Define activation energy.
(b) Write the unit of rate constant for
(i) zero order reaction, (ii) second order reaction.

key_points: (a) Activation energy is the minimum extra energy that reactant molecules must possess before they can react to form products.
(b)(i) Zero order: mol L–1 s–1
(b)(ii) Second order: L mol–1 s–1

questions.solution: Activation energy is the minimum amount of extra energy over and above the average energy of reactants that must be possessed by the colliding molecules for a fruitful collision to occur and for products to be formed. It represents the energy barrier that must be overcome for a reaction to proceed. For a zero order reaction, the rate = k[A]0 = k, and since rate has units of mol L–1 s–1, the unit of k for zero order is mol L–1 s–1. For a second order reaction, rate = k[A]2, so k = rate/[A]2 = (mol L–1 s–1)/(mol L–1)2 = L mol–1 s–1.
questions.topic: Activation energy and units of rate constant

questions.text:
(a) Zn की प्रथम आयनन एन्थैल्पी की तुलना में Cr की प्रथम आयनन एन्थैल्पी निम्न होती है। क्यों ?
(b) संक्रमण तत्वों के किसी एक गुणधर्म का उल्लेख कीजिए जो उन्हें एक उत्तम उत्प्रेरक बना देता है।
questions.text_english:
(a) First ionization enthalpy of Cr is lower than that of Zn. Why ?
(b) Mention any one property of the transition elements which makes them good catalysts.

key_points: (a) Zn has a completely filled 3d10 4s2 configuration, giving it extra stability, which makes it harder to remove an electron. Cr has a half-filled 3d5 4s1 configuration; the 4s1 electron is relatively easier to remove.
(b) Transition metals can exhibit variable oxidation states and provide a suitable surface for reactants to adsorb, making them good catalysts.

questions.solution: Zinc has the electronic configuration [Ar] 3d10 4s2. The completely filled 3d10 subshell provides extra stability to zinc, making its first ionization enthalpy higher. Chromium has [Ar] 3d5 4s1 with only one electron in the 4s orbital, which is comparatively easier to remove, resulting in a lower first ionization enthalpy. Transition metals make good catalysts because they can exhibit variable oxidation states and have the ability to form intermediate compounds. They also provide a surface for adsorption of reactant molecules, which increases the rate of reaction.
questions.topic: Ionization enthalpy and catalytic properties of transition metals

questions.text:
(a) उपसहसंयोजन संख्या की परिभाषा लिखिए।
(b) निम्नलिखित संकुल द्वारा प्रदर्शित समावयवता का प्रकार इंगित कीजिए :
[Co(en)3]Cl3
questions.text_english:
(a) Define coordination number.
(b) Indicate the type of isomerism exhibited by the following complex :
[Co(en)3]Cl3

key_points: (a) Coordination number is the number of ligand donor atoms directly bonded to the central metal atom or ion in a coordination complex.
(b) [Co(en)3]Cl3 exhibits optical isomerism (enantiomers — d and l forms).

questions.solution: The coordination number of a central metal atom in a coordination complex is defined as the total number of donor atoms of the ligands that are directly bonded to the central metal atom or ion. For example, in [Co(en)3]Cl3, ethylenediamine (en) is a bidentate ligand with two donor atoms, so the coordination number of Co is 6. The complex [Co(en)3]Cl3 is an octahedral tris-bidentate complex. questions.solution: The elevation in boiling point ΔTb = 353.93 – 353.23 = 0.70 K. questions.text_english:
(a) [Co(NH3)6]3+ is diamagnetic whereas [CoF6]3– is paramagnetic. Justify the statement. [Atomic number of Co = 27]
(b) Write the electronic configuration for d4 ion if Δ0 > P on the basis of crystal field theory.

key_points: (a) Co3+ has d6 configuration. NH3 is a strong field ligand causing complete pairing → t2g6 eg0, 0 unpaired electrons → diamagnetic. F– is a weak field ligand causing no forced pairing → t2g4 eg2 with 4 unpaired electrons → paramagnetic.

(b) When Δ0 > P (strong field), d4 ion: t2g3 eg1 is NOT correct; all 4 electrons pair in t2g level: t2g4 eg0 — wait, for d4 with strong field (Δ0>P): electrons fill t2g first, forcing pairing → t2g4 eg0, 2 unpaired electrons.

questions.solution: Co has atomic number 27, configuration [Ar] 3d7 4s2. Co3+ (loses 3 electrons) → [Ar] 3d6, a d6 ion. In [Co(NH3)6]3+, NH3 is a strong field ligand. The large crystal field splitting energy (Δ0 > pairing energy P) forces all 6 electrons to pair up in the lower t2g set: configuration t2g6 eg0 with zero unpaired electrons. Hence it is diamagnetic. In [CoF6]3–, F– is a weak field ligand (Δ0 < P), so electrons occupy orbitals with maximum spin (Hund's rule): t2g4 eg2, giving 4 unpaired electrons, making it paramagnetic. For a d4 ion with Δ0 > P (strong field/low spin case), all 4 electrons are forced into the lower t2g orbitals despite pairing: configuration is t2g4 eg0 with 2 unpaired electrons.

questions.solution: When cyclohexane reacts with Br2 in the presence of heat (or light), a free radical halogenation (substitution) reaction occurs. Write the reaction involved in

(b) Cannizzaro's reaction
(c) Hell – Volhard – Zelinsky reaction

key_points: (a) Rosenmund: RCOCl + H2 → RCHO + HCl (Pd/BaSO4 catalyst)
(b) Cannizzaro: 2HCHO + NaOH → CH3OH + HCOONa (disproportionation of aldehyde without α-H)

questions.solution: Rosenmund's reduction: An acid chloride (RCOCl) is reduced by H2 gas in the presence of Pd on BaSO4 catalyst (poisoned catalyst) to give an aldehyde: RCOCl + H2 → RCHO + HCl. Cannizzaro's reaction: Aldehydes lacking an α-hydrogen atom undergo self-disproportionation in concentrated alkali — one molecule is oxidized to the acid (carboxylate salt) and another is reduced to the alcohol. For example: 2HCHO + NaOH → CH3OH + HCOONa. Hell–Volhard–Zelinsky (HVZ) reaction: A carboxylic acid reacts with Br2 in the presence of red phosphorus to give α-brominated acid: CH3COOH + Br2 → CH2BrCOOH + HBr. The reaction occurs at the α-carbon position.

key_points: (A)(a) Reducing sugar: a sugar that can reduce Tollens' or Fehling's reagent because it has a free aldehyde or ketone group.
(A)(b)(i) Fibrous proteins: thread-like, insoluble, structural function (e.g. keratin, collagen). Globular proteins: spherical, soluble, metabolic functions (e.g. enzymes, hormones).
(A)(b)(ii) Nucleoside = nitrogenous base + pentose sugar. Nucleotide = nucleoside + phosphate group.
(B)(a) Glucose + H2NOH → Glucose oxime + H2O
(B)(b) Glucose + (CH3CO)2O → Glucose pentaacetate
(B)(c) Glucose + conc. HNO3 → Saccharic acid (glucaric acid)

questions.solution: Part A: A reducing sugar is one that can donate electrons to reduce other compounds, particularly Fehling's or Tollens' reagent. It contains a free or potentially free aldehyde or ketone group. Fibrous proteins are long, filamentous, water-insoluble proteins with structural roles (e.g. keratin in hair, collagen in tendons), while globular proteins are compact, roughly spherical, water-soluble proteins with dynamic roles such as enzymes and antibodies. A nucleoside consists of a nitrogenous base (purine or pyrimidine) covalently bonded to a pentose sugar (ribose or deoxyribose). A nucleotide is a nucleoside with one or more phosphate groups esterified to the sugar. Part B: (a) Glucose reacts with hydroxylamine (H2NOH) to form glucose oxime (CH=NOH group) and water. (b) Glucose reacts with acetic anhydride to form glucose pentaacetate, where all five –OH groups are acetylated. (c) Glucose reacts with concentrated HNO3 to form saccharic acid (glucaric acid), a dicarboxylic acid where both the –CHO and the terminal –CH2OH are oxidized to –COOH.

questions.text: परासरण वह प्रक्रम है जिसके द्वारा अर्धपारगम्य झिल्ली में से निम्न विलेय सांद्रता वाले विलयन की ओर से उच्च विलेय सांद्रता के विलयन की ओर विलायक अणुओं का प्रवाह होता है। परासरण दाब एक अणुसंख्य गुणधर्म है। जब विलयन पर परासरण दाब से अधिक दाब लगाया जाए तो प्रतिलोम परासरण हो जाता है। जब दो विलयन अर्धपारगम्य झिल्ली द्वारा पृथक किए गए हों और उनका परासरण दाब समान हो, तो उन्हें समपरासरी कहते हैं। पृथक किए दो विलयनों में से यदि एक का परासरण दाब निम्न हो तो उसे दूसरे विलयन के सापेक्ष अल्पपरासरी कहते हैं, यदि इसका परासरण दाब दूसरे विलयन की अपेक्षा अधिक हो तो उसे दूसरे विलयन के सापेक्ष अतिपरासरी कहते हैं। रुधिर कोशिका में स्थित द्रव का परासरण दाब 0.9% (द्रव्यमान/आयतन) सोडियम क्लोराइड, जिसे सामान्य लवण विलयन कहते हैं, के तुल्यांक होता है एवं इसे अंतः शिरा में अंतःक्षेपित (इंजेक्ट) करना सुरक्षित रहता है। दैनिक जीवन एवं प्रकृति में परासरण दाब महत्वपूर्ण होता है।
questions.text_english: Osmosis is a process by which the molecules of a solvent pass from a solution of low solute concentration to a solution of high solute concentration through a semi-permeable membrane. Osmotic pressure is a colligative property. When the applied pressure on a solution exceeds its osmotic pressure, reverse osmosis occurs. When two solutions are separated by a semipermeable membrane and they have same osmotic pressure they are said to be isotonic. Of the two solutions separated by a semipermeable membrane, if one is a lower osmotic pressure, it is said to be hypotonic relative to the second solution. If it has a higher osmotic pressure, than the second solution, it is said to be hypertonic relative to the second solution. The osmotic pressure associated with the fluid inside the blood cell is equivalent to that of 0.9% (mass/volume) sodium chloride solution called normal saline solution and it is safe to inject intravenously. Osmotic pressure is vital in daily life and nature. It helps in explain, why IV fluids match blood's osmotic pressure, its also the principle behind food preservation using salt or sugar.

Calculate the amount of CaCl2 (i = 2.59) dissolved in 2.46 litre of water such that its osmotic pressure is 0.70 atm at 27°C.
[Given : R = 0.082 L atm K–1 mol–1, molar mass of CaCl2 = 111 g mol–1]
sub_questions.solution: Using the modified osmotic pressure equation for electrolytes: π = iCRT, where π = 0.70 atm, i = 2.59, R = 0.082 L atm K–1 mol–1, T = 27 + 273 = 300 K. Molar concentration C = π/(iRT) = 0.70/(2.59 × 0.082 × 300) = 0.70/63.726 = 0.010983 mol L–1. Moles of CaCl2 = C × V = 0.010983 × 2.46 = 0.02702 mol. Mass of CaCl2 = moles × molar mass = 0.02702 × 111 = 2.999 g ≈ 3 g.

questions.text_english: Like NH3, nitrogen atom of amine is trivalent and carries an unshared pair of electrons. Nitrogen orbitals in amines are therefore sp3 hybridised and the geometry of amines is pyramidal. Lower aliphatic amines are soluble in water due to the formation of hydrogen bond with water molecules. The solubility decreases as the molar mass of amines increases due to increase in size of hydrophobic part. Higher amines are insoluble in water. However amines are less soluble in water than alcohols because of low electronegativity of nitrogen as compared to oxygen. Boiling points of isomeric amines follow the order 1° > 2° > 3°. It is due to the fact the amines are held together due to hydrogen bonding. Extent of hydrogen bonding is more in primary amines than in secondary amines as two hydrogen atoms are available for hydrogen bond formation. Tertiary amines do not show hydrogen bonding because of the absence of hydrogen atom attached to nitrogen. Amines can be prepared from, nitro compounds, nitriles, amides etc.

sub_questions.text_english: Why primary amines have higher boiling points than tertiary amines ?

key_points: Primary amines have N–H bonds and can form intermolecular hydrogen bonds extensively (two H atoms available), raising the boiling point. Tertiary amines have no N–H bonds and hence no hydrogen bonding, resulting in lower boiling points.

sub_questions.solution: Primary amines have two hydrogen atoms attached to the nitrogen atom, which allows them to form extensive intermolecular hydrogen bonds (N–H···N). These hydrogen bonds require additional energy to break during boiling, resulting in higher boiling points. Tertiary amines have no hydrogen atom on the nitrogen (all three hydrogens are replaced by alkyl/aryl groups), so they cannot form hydrogen bonds. Therefore, tertiary amines have much lower boiling points than primary amines of comparable molecular mass.

questions.solution: Part A(a): (i) Propanone is converted to propene by first reducing it to propan-2-ol using NaBH4 or LiAlH4, then dehydrating propan-2-ol with concentrated H2SO4 at 443 K to give propene. (ii) Benzoic acid is converted to benzaldehyde via benzoyl chloride: treat benzoic acid with SOCl2 to form benzoyl chloride (C6H5COCl), then perform Rosenmund reduction using H2 over Pd/BaSO4 catalyst. (iii) Benzene is first acetylated using CH3COCl and anhydrous AlCl3 (Friedel-Crafts acylation) to give acetophenone; acetophenone is then nitrated with a mixture of concentrated HNO3 and H2SO4. Since –COCH3 is a meta-director, nitration occurs at the meta position to give m-nitroacetophenone. Part A(b): (i) Reactivity of carbonyl compounds towards HCN decreases with increasing steric hindrance. The bulkier the groups around C=O, the less reactive it is. Order (increasing reactivity): di-t-butyl ketone < acetone < acetaldehyde, i.e., (CH3)3CCOC(CH3)3 < CH3COCH3 < CH3CHO. (ii) Aldol condensation requires the presence of at least one α-hydrogen. HCHO (formaldehyde) has no α-carbon, C6H5CHO has no α-hydrogen, so these cannot undergo aldol condensation. CH3CHO (acetaldehyde) and cyclopentanone both have α-hydrogens, so they undergo aldol condensation. Part B(a): (i) Iodoform test: acetophenone (methyl ketone, CH3COC6H5) gives a yellow iodoform precipitate with I2/NaOH; benzophenone does not. (ii) Tollen's test (silver mirror test): propanal gives a silver mirror (aldehyde is oxidized); propanone (ketone) does not react. (iii) Iodoform test: pentan-2-one (CH3COCH2CH2CH3) is a methyl ketone and gives yellow iodoform precipitate; pentan-3-one (CH3CH2COCH2CH3) does not. Part B(b): (i) CH2FCOOH is stronger than CH3COOH because fluorine is highly electronegative and exerts a strong electron-withdrawing inductive effect (–I effect), which stabilizes the carboxylate anion and facilitates dissociation. (ii) Boiling point order: CH3CH2CH3 (propane, no polarity, only van der Waals) < CH3OCH3 (dimethyl ether, polar but no H-bonding) < CH3CHO (acetaldehyde, polar, no H-bonding with self) < CH3CH2OH (ethanol, strong H-bonding).

(A) (a) The conductivity of 0.1 mol L–1 solution of NaCl is 1.06 × 10–2 S cm–1. Calculate its molar conductivity and degree of dissociation.
λ°Na+ = 50.1 S cm2 mol–1, λ°Cl– = 76.5 S cm2 mol–1
(b) (i) Following cell reaction occurs in a galvanic cell :
2Ag+(aq) + Zn(s) → 2Ag(s) + Zn2+(aq) E°(cell) = +1.56 V
Predict the direction of flow of current.
(ii) Differentiate between a primary battery and a secondary battery.
OR
(B) (a) Resistance of a conductivity cell filled with 0.1 M KCl solution is 100 Ω. If the resistance of the same cell when filled with 0.01 mol L–1 KCl solution is 300 Ω, calculate the conductivity and molar conductivity of 0.01 mol L–1 KCl solution. The conductivity of 0.1 M KCl solution is 1.29 × 10–2 S cm–1.
(b) (i) Write any two advantages of H2–O2 fuel cell.
(ii) Why does the cell potential of mercury cell remain constant throughout the life ?

key_points: (A)(b)(i) Current flows from Ag electrode (cathode, higher reduction potential) to Zn electrode (anode) in the external circuit, i.e., from cathode to anode externally (conventional current from Ag to Zn in external circuit).

(A)(b)(ii) Primary battery: cannot be recharged; cell reaction is irreversible (e.g. dry cell). Secondary battery: can be recharged by passing electric current in reverse; cell reaction is reversible (e.g. lead storage battery).
(B)(b)(i) H2-O2 fuel cell: high efficiency (~70%), produces water as the only byproduct (eco-friendly), continuous operation as long as fuel is supplied.
(B)(b)(ii) Mercury cell: Zn-HgO cell; the electrolyte (KOH/ZnO) concentration does not change during the reaction, keeping E°cell constant throughout.

questions.solution: Part A(a): Molar conductivity Λm = κ × 1000/M = (1.06 × 10–2 × 1000)/0.1 = 106 S cm2 mol–1. Limiting molar conductivity Λ°m(NaCl) = λ°Na+ + λ°Cl– = 50.1 + 76.5 = 126.6 S cm2 mol–1. Degree of dissociation α = Λm/Λ°m = 106/126.6 = 0.837 (83.7%). Part A(b)(i): In the galvanic cell, Zn is oxidized at the anode and Ag+ is reduced at the cathode. Conventional current flows from cathode (Ag) to anode (Zn) in the external circuit, i.e., current flows from the Ag electrode to the Zn electrode externally. Part A(b)(ii): Primary batteries like dry cells cannot be recharged because their cell reactions are irreversible; once the reactants are consumed the battery is discarded. Secondary batteries like lead-acid accumulators can be recharged by applying an external electric current that reverses the cell reaction, restoring the original reactants. Part B(a): Cell constant G* = κ × R = 1.29 × 10–2 × 100 = 1.29 cm–1. κ(0.01 M KCl) = G*/R = 1.29/300 = 4.3 × 10–3 S cm–1. Λm = (κ × 1000)/C = (4.3 × 10–3 × 1000)/0.01 = 430 S cm2 mol–1. Part B(b)(i): Two advantages of H2–O2 fuel cell: (1) Very high efficiency (~70%) compared to conventional thermal power. (2) The only byproduct is water, making it pollution-free and environmentally friendly. Part B(b)(ii): The mercury cell uses the reaction Zn(Hg) + HgO → ZnO + Hg. The electrolyte (KOH/ZnO paste) concentration does not change during the operation because no ions are consumed or produced in solution; the cell reaction involves only solid-state changes. Since the concentration remains constant, the cell potential remains constant throughout the life of the battery.

(b) Explain the mechanism of acid catalyzed hydration of alkene to form corresponding alcohol.

key_points: A = Ethanol (C2H5OH); reacts with Na → B = Sodium ethoxide (C2H5ONa) + H2
A + I2/NaOH → C = CHI3 (Iodoform, yellow precipitate) + sodium formate
A + H2SO4 (413 K) → D = Diethyl ether (C4H10O, C2H5OC2H5)
D + excess HI → E = Ethyl iodide (C2H5I) + ethanol (cleavage of ether)
(B)(a)(i) Phenol + Br2(aq) → 2,4,6-tribromophenol (reagent: bromine water)
(B)(a)(ii) Propene + H2O → propan-1-ol (reagent: B2H6/H2O2/NaOH, hydroboration-oxidation, anti-Markovnikov)

questions.solution: Part A: Compound A (C2H6O) reacts with sodium to give H2 gas, indicating the presence of an –OH group; A is ethanol (C2H5OH). Reaction 1: 2C2H5OH + 2Na → 2C2H5ONa (B, sodium ethoxide) + H2. Reaction 2: C2H5OH + I2 + NaOH → CHI3 (C, iodoform — yellow precipitate) + HCOONa + NaI + H2O. This is the iodoform reaction, confirming the CH3CH(OH)– group. Reaction 3: 2C2H5OH + H2SO4 at 413 K → C2H5OC2H5 (D, diethyl ether, C4H10O) + H2O. Reaction 4: C2H5OC2H5 + excess HI → 2C2H5I (E, ethyl iodide). So A = ethanol, B = sodium ethoxide, C = iodoform (CHI3), D = diethyl ether, E = ethyl iodide. Part B(a): (i) Phenol to 2,4,6-tribromophenol: reagent is bromine water (Br2/H2O) — electrophilic aromatic substitution occurs at all three ortho/para positions. (ii) Propene to propan-1-ol: reagent is diborane (B2H6) followed by H2O2/NaOH (hydroboration-oxidation) — anti-Markovnikov addition. (iii) Butan-2-one to butan-2-ol: reagent is NaBH4 (or LiAlH4) — reduction of ketone to secondary alcohol. Part B(b): Mechanism of acid-catalyzed hydration of alkene — Step 1: The H+ ion (from dilute H2SO4 or H3PO4) protonates the alkene at the less-substituted carbon (following Markovnikov's rule) to form a more stable carbocation. Step 2: A water molecule acts as a nucleophile and attacks the carbocation to form a protonated alcohol (oxonium ion). Step 3: The oxonium ion loses a proton to a water molecule to regenerate H+ and form the alcohol product. The overall process follows Markovnikov's rule.
